collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Cholera from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Cholera.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.
The extraction_record_model is flagged as still hantavirus-named (task_input_warnings) — verify field mappings are correctly applied to cholera schema before extraction.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Cholera from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Cholera.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP Haiti is the primary national authority publishing weekly and monthly cholera bulletins with subnational (departmental) case, death, and hospitalization counts. Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 provide case definitions, serotype/biotype data, and methodological context for interpreting surveillance counts. May also contain original case series data.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse) and humanitarian news services (ReliefWeb, IRIN) may contain early outbreak signals, subnational case reports, and situation summaries for Haiti cholera 2024, particularly during periods of official reporting gaps.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.
The extraction_record_model is flagged as still hantavirus-named (task_input_warnings) — verify field mappings are correctly applied to cholera schema before extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP Haiti is the primary national authority publishing weekly and monthly cholera bulletins with subnational (departmental) case, death, and hospitalization counts. count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

WHO, OCHA, UNICEF, and MSF publish Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates that contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization data, often with departmental breakdowns. These serve as both primary collection and cross-validation sources.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 provide case definitions, serotype/biotype data, and methodological context for interpreting surveillance counts. May also contain original case series data.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse) and humanitarian news services (ReliefWeb, IRIN) may contain early outbreak signals, subnational case reports, and situation summaries for Haiti cholera 2024, particularly during periods of official reporting gaps.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP Haiti is the primary national authority publishing weekly and monthly cholera bulletins with subnational (departmental) case, death, and hospitalization counts. PAHO/AMRO publishes Haiti-specific cholera situation reports with similar granularity. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024 window.

WHO, OCHA, UNICEF, and MSF publish Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates that contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization data, often with departmental breakdowns. These serve as both primary collection and cross-validation sources.

WHO Global Health Observatory, Global Infectious Disease and Epidemiology Network (GIDEON), ProMED, and HealthMap provide structured or semi-structured Haiti cholera records useful for validation cross-checks against collected data.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 provide case definitions, serotype/biotype data, and methodological context for interpreting surveillance counts. May also contain original case series data.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse) and humanitarian news services (ReliefWeb, IRIN) may contain early outbreak signals, subnational case reports, and situation summaries for Haiti cholera 2024, particularly during periods of official reporting gaps.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.
The extraction_record_model is flagged as still hantavirus-named (task_input_warnings) — verify field mappings are correctly applied to cholera schema before extraction.
source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic (task_input_warnings) — source discovery logic may need manual override for cholera-specific sources.
WHO Global Cholera Dashboard may lag behind MSPP primary reporting by days to weeks — use MSPP as primary, WHO/PAHO as validation.
Locality-level data (commune, quartier) may be sparse or inconsistently reported — flag missing locality as NULL rather than inferring.
CFR values above 2% in any subnational unit may indicate reporting anomalies or access-constrained areas — flag for review.
Do not invent or infer source URLs — source_url must be populated only from directly observed source metadata.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Cholera.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP Haiti is the primary national authority publishing weekly and monthly cholera bulletins with subnational (departmental) case, death, and hospitalization counts. PAHO/AMRO publishes Haiti-specific cholera situation reports with similar granularity. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024 window.

WHO, OCHA, UNICEF, and MSF publish Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates that contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization data, often with departmental breakdowns. These serve as both primary collection and cross-validation sources.

WHO Global Health Observatory, Global Infectious Disease and Epidemiology Network (GIDEON), ProMED, and HealthMap provide structured or semi-structured Haiti cholera records useful for validation cross-checks against collected data.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 provide case definitions, serotype/biotype data, and methodological context for interpreting surveillance counts. May also contain original case series data.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse) and humanitarian news services (ReliefWeb, IRIN) may contain early outbreak signals, subnational case reports, and situation summaries for Haiti cholera 2024, particularly during periods of official reporting gaps.

iterative_search_queries.query: MSPP choléra Haïti 2024 bulletin épidémiologique cas décès
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: MSPP is the primary national authority for cholera surveillance in Haiti. Their bulletins ('bulletins épidémiologiques') are the gold-standard source for subnational case/death breakdowns. French-language query with MSPP name and key epidemiological terms maximizes recall against their document corpus. Upstream queries did not explicitly name MSPP.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletins, cholera situation reports, or surveillance summaries published on mspp.gouv.ht or affiliated portals
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Official Haitian government health ministry domain (mspp.gouv.ht), French-language bulletin with case/death counts by department or commune

iterative_search_queries.query: PAHO WHO cholera Haiti 2024 situation report cases deaths epidemiological update
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: PAHO is the WHO regional office for the Americas and publishes regular cholera situation reports for Haiti, often with subnational breakdowns and cumulative totals. WHO DONs provide internationally validated outbreak summaries. Explicitly naming both PAHO and WHO improves retrieval of these high-authority sources. Upstream queries used generic 'outbreak report surveillance' without agency names.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO/AMRO situation reports, WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO GTFCC cholera updates, or PAHO epidemiological alerts for Haiti 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: paho.org or who.int domain, official situation report or DON format with cumulative or weekly case/death counts

iterative_search_queries.query: Haiti cholera 2024 cases deaths ReliefWeb OCHA humanitarian situation report
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: ReliefWeb aggregates OCHA, UNICEF, MSF, and other humanitarian actor reports on Haiti cholera. These often contain subnational breakdowns and time-series data not easily found via direct agency searches. OCHA Haiti publishes regular situation reports that include MSPP-sourced cholera statistics. This channel was not explicitly targeted in upstream queries.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: OCHA Haiti situation reports on ReliefWeb, UNICEF humanitarian situation reports, MSF/IRC field reports with cholera case counts, or OCHA Flash Updates referencing cholera data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: reliefweb.int or unocha.org domain, humanitarian situation report format with epidemiological figures attributed to MSPP or PAHO

iterative_search_queries.query: WHO Global Health Observatory cholera Haiti 2024 surveillance data annual cases deaths
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: The WHO GHO and GTFCC maintain structured annual cholera surveillance datasets by country. The WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record publishes annual cholera tables. These provide validated aggregate figures for Haiti 2024 that can anchor and cross-check subnational data from MSPP/PAHO. Upstream queries used generic 'surveillance dataset' phrasing without naming these specific WHO data products.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) cholera dataset, WHO GTFCC (Global Task Force on Cholera Control) annual data, or WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record (WER) cholera tables for Haiti 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: who.int/data or apps.who.int domain, structured tabular data with country-level annual or quarterly cholera statistics

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Cholera.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP Haiti is the primary national authority publishing weekly and monthly cholera bulletins with subnational (departmental) case, death, and hospitalization counts. PAHO/AMRO publishes Haiti-specific cholera situation reports with similar granularity. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024 window.

WHO, OCHA, UNICEF, and MSF publish Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates that contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization data, often with departmental breakdowns. These serve as both primary collection and cross-validation sources.

WHO Global Health Observatory, Global Infectious Disease and Epidemiology Network (GIDEON), ProMED, and HealthMap provide structured or semi-structured Haiti cholera records useful for validation cross-checks against collected data.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 provide case definitions, serotype/biotype data, and methodological context for interpreting surveillance counts. May also contain original case series data.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse) and humanitarian news services (ReliefWeb, IRIN) may contain early outbreak signals, subnational case reports, and situation summaries for Haiti cholera 2024, particularly during periods of official reporting gaps.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP Haiti is the primary national authority publishing weekly and monthly cholera bulletins with subnational (departmental) case, death, and hospitalization counts. PAHO/AMRO publishes Haiti-specific cholera situation reports with similar granularity. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024 window.

WHO, OCHA, UNICEF, and MSF publish Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates that contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization data, often with departmental breakdowns. These serve as both primary collection and cross-validation sources.

WHO Global Health Observatory, Global Infectious Disease and Epidemiology Network (GIDEON), ProMED, and HealthMap provide structured or semi-structured Haiti cholera records useful for validation cross-checks against collected data.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 provide case definitions, serotype/biotype data, and methodological context for interpreting surveillance counts. May also contain original case series data.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse) and humanitarian news services (ReliefWeb, IRIN) may contain early outbreak signals, subnational case reports, and situation summaries for Haiti cholera 2024, particularly during periods of official reporting gaps.

disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (Haiti)", "departmental (e.g., Artibonite, Ouest, Nord, Sud, Centre, Grand'Anse, Nippes, Nord-Est, Nord-Ouest, Sud-Est)", "communal/municipal", "locality/quartier"]
count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) Haiti official cholera bulletins, situation reports, and surveillance data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts. Weekly and monthly bulletins are the highest-priority collection targets.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/AMRO cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, and Haiti-specific cholera data pages for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO regularly publishes Haiti cholera situation reports with subnational breakdowns, case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. These are primary collection sources when MSPP data is unavailable or incomplete.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Dashboard entries and WHO situation reports covering Haiti for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO publishes global cholera dashboards and country-level situation reports that include Haiti case and death counts, often with temporal granularity useful for the 2024 window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify OCHA Haiti humanitarian situation reports and flash updates referencing cholera case or death counts for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: OCHA Haiti publishes humanitarian situation reports that frequently cite cholera figures from MSPP and PAHO, providing additional subnational and temporal granularity.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti cholera-related situation reports and humanitarian response updates for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF Haiti publishes situation reports and humanitarian dashboards that include cholera case and death data, often with departmental breakdowns.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., WHO Global Health Observatory, ProMED, HealthMap) with Haiti cholera records for 2024 to use as held-back validation sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validating extracted case and death counts without leaking into primary collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) operational reports and cholera treatment center data for Haiti 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSF operates cholera treatment centers in Haiti and publishes operational data that can serve as an independent validation source for hospitalization and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and epidemiological studies on Haiti cholera 2024 for case definition context and count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, methodology, and epidemiological context needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted counts (confirmed vs. suspected vs. AWD).

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WASH cluster reports and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) surveillance summaries for Haiti 2024 to contextualize syndrome-based counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: AWD and WASH cluster reports help distinguish cholera-specific counts from broader diarrheal disease surveillance, critical for correct field mapping.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident, suspected vs. confirmed) or unclear subnational attribution for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reporting in 2024 may mix cumulative totals from the 2022 re-emergence with new 2024 incident counts. Human review is required to resolve temporal and definitional ambiguities.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where gang violence, infrastructure collapse, or access restrictions may have caused reporting gaps or underreporting in specific departments during 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti experienced severe security deterioration in 2024, particularly in Ouest/Port-au-Prince. Reporting gaps in affected departments must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero counts.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish between cumulative and incident (new/weekly) case counts — Haitian MSPP bulletins typically report both cumulative and weekly figures.
Confirmed cases require laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR for Vibrio cholerae O1/O139); suspected cases are clinical/epidemiological definitions only.
Case fatality rate (CFR) should be computed from confirmed or total reported cases and deaths — verify denominator used by source.
PAHO and WHO may aggregate or smooth data differently from MSPP primary bulletins — note source hierarchy.
Hospitalization counts may reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions — clarify in evidence_quote.
Some sources report 'acute watery diarrhea' (AWD) counts that may include non-cholera cases — flag if pathogen confirmation is absent.
Subnational data may be reported as cumulative departmental totals; locality-level data may only appear in MSF or OCHA field reports.
disambiguation_risks: AWD (acute watery diarrhea) counts may conflate cholera with other enteric pathogens — require pathogen confirmation or source clarification.
Haiti cholera data may be reported under 'cholera' and separately under 'AWD' by different agencies — avoid double-counting.
MSPP bulletins are in French — ensure translation accuracy for case classification terms (cas confirmé vs. cas suspect vs. cas probable).
Cumulative vs. incident counts: sources may not always clearly label whether figures are new (weekly/monthly) or cumulative — extract and label both if present.
Departmental names in French (e.g., 'Artibonite', 'Ouest') must be standardized to English equivalents for subnational_location field.
Post-2022 cholera resurgence in Haiti may produce overlapping epidemic waves — ensure date ranges are precisely captured per record.
MSF and OCHA field reports may cover sub-periods or specific localities not aligned with MSPP national reporting periods — note temporal scope per source.
warnings: MSPP Haiti bulletins are published in French — bilingual query strategy required.
Haiti experienced a major cholera resurgence beginning in late 2022; 2024 data must be carefully scoped to avoid inclusion of 2022–2023 cumulative figures.
Security and access constraints in Haiti (gang activity, displacement) may cause reporting gaps or delays in subnational data for 2024.
Some MSPP bulletins may not be publicly archived or may have irregular publication schedules — cross-validate with PAHO/WHO sitreps.
The extraction_record_model is flagged as still hantavirus-named (task_input_warnings) — verify field mappings are correctly applied to cholera schema before extraction.
source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic (task_input_warnings) — source discovery logic may need manual override for cholera-specific sources.
WHO Global Cholera Dashboard may lag behind MSPP primary reporting by days to weeks — use MSPP as primary, WHO/PAHO as validation.
Locality-level data (commune, quartier) may be sparse or inconsistently reported — flag missing locality as NULL rather than inferring.
CFR values above 2% in any subnational unit may indicate reporting anomalies or access-constrained areas — flag for review.
Do not invent or infer source URLs — source_url must be populated only from directly observed source metadata.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Cholera.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
